dish.title: Filipino Pork Menudo with Potatoes, Carrots, Raisins, and Rice
dish.description: Pork shoulder marinated briefly in soy sauce and lemon juice, browned with garlic and onion, then simmered in tomato sauce with diced potatoes, carrots, red bell pepper, raisins, and bay until thick, served with long-grain rice.

recipe_version.title: Filipino Pork Menudo with Potatoes, Carrots, Raisins, and Rice
recipe_version.description: Pork shoulder marinated briefly in soy sauce and lemon juice, browned with garlic and onion, then simmered in tomato sauce with diced potatoes, carrots, red bell pepper, raisins, and bay until thick, served with long-grain rice.

ingredients.name: tomato sauce
ingredients.display_name: tomato sauce (one 8-oz can) whose label lists tomatoes, salt, and spices

steps.title: Prep and marinate
steps.body: Cube the pork and toss it in the medium bowl with the soy sauce and lemon juice; let it sit while you dice the onion, potatoes, carrots, and bell pepper, mince the garlic, and rinse the rice.

steps.title: Brown the pork
steps.body: Heat the oil in the 5.5-quart Dutch oven over medium-high, about 2 minutes. Lift the pork from the marinade (save it) and brown it, about 8 minutes.

steps.title: Aromatics and sauce
steps.body: Add the garlic and onion and cook until soft, about 4 minutes. Stir in the tomato sauce, the saved marinade, 1 1/2 cups water, and the bay leaves.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.body: Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low until the pork is nearly tender, about 35 minutes. Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer covered 15 minutes, then the bell pepper, raisins, salt, and pepper and simmer uncovered until thick, about 6 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: During the last 30 minutes of the simmer (overlap stated): combine the rice and 2 1/4 cups water in the lidded 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes. Rest covered off the heat 10 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Discard the bay leaves and serve the menudo beside the rice.

coverage_contribution: Filipino food in the catalog is chicken adobo only. A homestyle tomato pork stew adds a second Filipino dish and a pork dinner.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with filipino-chicken-adobo: pork in tomato sauce with potatoes, carrots, and raisins, not chicken braised in vinegar and soy. Compared with cuban-picadillo-rice: cubed pork stew with potatoes, not ground beef with olives. Compared with slow-cooker-ropa-vieja: a stovetop soy-tomato pork stew, not shredded slow-cooked beef.
not_duplicate_of: Not Mexican menudo (no tripe or hominy) and not pork afritada (raisins and smaller dice).
